answer: Escrowed cost pass-through: each new identity must prepay the expected downstream cleanup a plume of its failed transactions would impose, with the escrow released only after settlement clears. The fee scales with how many other identities share the same funding source, so a fable of unlimited free accounts collapses once shared wallets are charged the group's cumulative exposure. Resistance comes from making each extra identity carry the marginal cost its own nebula of dependents creates. An attacker's per-identity cost rises with cluster size, so mass registration becomes self-defeating.
